# frozen_string_literal: true

module Api
  module V1
    # Every v1 controller hangs off this one.
    #
    # The seller console is a browser client on a sibling origin, so its session
    # rides in a signed HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie; the mobile clients present
    # the same opaque token as a bearer header instead. Either way we store only
    # the digest, so a database dump hands nobody a live session.
    class BaseController < ActionController::API
      include ActionController::Cookies

      class Unauthenticated < StandardError; end

      before_action :authenticate_seller!

      rescue_from Unauthenticated do
        render json: { error: "unauthenticated" }, status: :unauthorized
      end

      rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound do
        render json: { error: "not_found" }, status: :not_found
      end

      rescue_from ActionController::ParameterMissing do |error|
        render json: { error: "invalid_request", parameter: error.param }, status: :bad_request
      end

      private

      def authenticate_seller!
        digest = OpenSSL::Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(presented_token)
        session = SellerSession.active.find_by(token_digest: digest)
        raise Unauthenticated if session.nil?

        Current.seller = session.seller
        Current.session = session
        session.touch(:last_seen_at)
      end

      # A bearer token is presented deliberately by a client that had to read it
      # first. A cookie is presented by the browser whether the request was meant
      # or not, so it is only honoured alongside a header carrying the same value
      # — a cross-site submission arrives with the cookie and without the header,
      # and stops here.
      def presented_token
        header = request.headers["Authorization"].to_s
        return header.delete_prefix("Bearer ") if header.start_with?("Bearer ")

        cookie = cookies.signed[:seller_session].to_s
        raise Unauthenticated if cookie.blank?
        unless ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(request.headers["X-Session-Token"].to_s, cookie)
          raise Unauthenticated
        end

        cookie
      end
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Api
  # Turns "this record exists" into "this record is yours".
  #
  # A controller includes this *after* the callback that loads its member record,
  # so the ownership check is appended to the callback chain and runs once the
  # record is in place. Including it above the loader would check a nil and 404
  # every request, which is at least the safe direction to get it wrong in.
  module SellerOwned
    extend ActiveSupport::Concern

    included do
      before_action :enforce_seller_ownership!, only: %i[show update destroy verification]
    end

    private

    # A record belonging to somebody else is reported exactly as a record that
    # does not exist, so ids stay unenumerable.
    def enforce_seller_ownership!
      record = instance_variable_get(:"@#{controller_name.singularize}")
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound if record.nil?
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless record.seller_id == Current.seller.id
    end
  end
end

cases.why: The loader is the same unscoped `PayoutMethod.find(params[:id])` as its vulnerable sibling, but ownership is enforced two files away: `include Api::SellerOwned` is placed deliberately after the loader's before_action so the concern's `enforce_seller_ownership!` is appended behind it in the callback chain and runs on a populated @payout_method. A record belonging to another seller raises RecordNotFound before any action body executes.

# frozen_string_literal: true

# Columns, for anyone reading a controller that writes to this table:
#
#   seller_id            bigint    not null
#   title                string
#   subtitle             string
#   description          text
#   price_cents          integer
#   currency             string
#   condition            string
#   quantity             integer
#   status               string    pending_review | live | suspended
#   review_state         string    written by the trust team, never by a seller
#   commission_rate_bps  integer   per-listing override of the 900bps default
#   featured_until       datetime  paid placement, written by the ads worker
#   payout_hold          boolean   set when trust and safety freeze a seller
class Listing < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :seller
  has_many :listing_categories, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :categories, through: :listing_categories
  has_many_attached :photos

  enum :status, { pending_review: "pending_review", live: "live", suspended: "suspended" }

  validates :title, presence: true, length: { maximum: 140 }
  validates :price_cents, numericality: { greater_than: 0, less_than: 500_000_00 }
  validates :quantity, numericality: { greater_than_or_equal_to: 0 }
  validates :currency, inclusion: { in: %w[EUR GBP USD] }

  scope :sellable, -> { where(status: "live").where(quantity: 1..) }
end

cases.why: `listing_params` calls `permit!`, so #update assigns every key the client sends. The listings table (see app/models/listing.rb) carries `status`, `review_state`, `commission_rate_bps`, `featured_until` and `payout_hold` alongside the editable fields, none of which has a validation that would stop a seller from publishing an unreviewed listing, zeroing their own commission or buying themselves paid placement. #create on the same controller still uses an explicit permit list, so the drift is visible in one file.

    # Every v1 controller hangs off this one.
    #
    # The seller console is a browser client on a sibling origin, so its session
    # rides in a signed HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie; the mobile clients present
    # the same opaque token as a bearer header instead. Either way we store only
    # the digest, so a database dump hands nobody a live session.
    class BaseController < ActionController::API

        render json: { error: "unauthenticated" }, status: :unauthorized

        render json: { error: "not_found" }, status: :not_found
      end

      rescue_from ActionController::ParameterMissing do |error|

      end

        session = SellerSession.active.find_by(token_digest: digest)

        Current.session = session
        session.touch(:last_seen_at)

      # first. A cookie is presented by the browser whether the request was meant
      # or not, so it is only honoured alongside a header carrying the same value
      # — a cross-site submission arrives with the cookie and without the header,
      # and stops here.

# frozen_string_literal: true

# The OAuth `state` parameter, as a message signed with the application's own
# key.
#
# A verified token proves the callback belongs to a flow this application
# started, and that nobody edited the payload in transit. It says nothing about
# whether the *values* inside the payload are acceptable — they came from the
# client that started the flow.
module StateToken
  class Invalid < StandardError; end

  TTL = 10.minutes

  def self.issue(payload)
    verifier.generate(payload.stringify_keys, expires_in: TTL, purpose: :oauth_state)
  end

  def self.verify!(token)
    verifier.verified(token.to_s, purpose: :oauth_state) || raise(Invalid, "state did not verify")
  end

  def self.verifier
    Rails.application.message_verifier(:oauth_state)
  end
end

cases.why: The callback redirects to `payload["return_to"]` with `allow_other_host: true`, which is the flag a developer reaches for the moment Rails 7's open-redirect guard fires. The comment's reasoning is the defect: the signature proves we minted the state, and we minted it from `params[:return_to]` on the connect call without checking it, so anyone who can send a seller to /connect?return_to=… controls where the browser lands immediately after a successful account link — the highest-trust moment in the flow.

# frozen_string_literal: true

# Prepares a parameter hash for an application log line.
#
# The list is an allow-list rather than a deny-list on purpose: a field nobody
# has classified yet is redacted by default, so adding a column to a form cannot
# quietly widen what reaches the log drain. `config.filter_parameters` covers the
# request log Rails writes for us; it does nothing for a line we write ourselves,
# which is what this is for.
module Redaction
  LOGGABLE_KEYS = %w[
    form_kind country_code region_code locale consent_version
    submitted_from entity_type has_dependents
  ].freeze

  FILTERED = "[filtered]"

  def self.scrub(hash)
    hash.each_with_object({}) do |(key, value), out|
      out[key.to_s] = LOGGABLE_KEYS.include?(key.to_s) ? value : FILTERED
    end
  end
end

cases.why: The log line is character-for-character the shape of its vulnerable sibling, `payload=#{...to_h.inspect}` included, but the hash goes through `Redaction.scrub` first. That helper is an allow-list: a key not named in LOGGABLE_KEYS is replaced with "[filtered]", so the taxpayer identification number, VAT number and address are unreachable by construction and a newly added form field is redacted by default rather than leaked by default.
